The '''Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry''', sometimes referred to as the '''Northwest derby''', is a high-profile inter-city rivalry between English professional [[association football]] clubs [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. It is considered one of the biggest fixtures in English football and one of the biggest and fiercest rivalries in world football.<ref>{{multiref2

}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Biggest Soccer Rivalries in the World |url=https://www.bootsnall.com/articles/biggest-soccer-rivalries-world.html |access-date=21 April 2022 |website=bootsnall.com}}</ref> Players, fans and the media consider the fixture between the two clubs to be their biggest rivalry, above even their own local derbies, with [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] respectively.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-remain-manchester-uniteds-biggest-rival-says-ryan-giggs-8390079.html |title=Liverpool remain Manchester United's 'biggest rival' says Ryan Giggs |work=The Independent|date=6 December 2012 |access-date=7 November 2015 }}</ref><ref name="Wilson 2020">{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Paul |title=Klopp ready for Liverpool's 'biggest game' against Manchester United |website=The Guardian |date=18 January 2020 |url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jan/18/jurgen-klopp-biggest-game-liverpool-manchester-united |access-date=7 February 2021}}</ref><ref name="Ganley 2019">{{cite web |last=Ganley |first=Joe |title=De Gea: This game is very different and unique |website=Manchester United |date=23 February 2019 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/printproduct/detail/david-de-gea-says-manchester-united-v-liverpool-is-the-biggest-fixture-in-english-football |access-date=7 February 2021}}</ref>

The rivalry has been fuelled by the [[Liverpool–Manchester rivalry|proximity of the two major cities]] that they represent, their historic economic and industrial rivalry, significant periods of domestic footballing dominance and European success, and their popularity at home and abroad, as two of the biggest-earning and widely supported football clubs in the world.<ref name=BusinessInsider2>{{cite news |first=Nick |last=Harris |title=MAN UNITED AND LIVERPOOL REMAIN TOP TV DRAWS DESPITE 2013–14 WITHOUT TROPHIES|url=http://www.sportingintelligence.com/2014/07/21/man-united-and-liverpool-remain-top-tv-draws-despite-2013-14-without-trophies-210703/|publisher=Sporting Intelligence |date=21 July 2014 |access-date=7 November 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd drops down wealth league |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/6339941.stm |website=BBC News |date=8 February 2007 |access-date=22 August 2012 }}</ref><ref name=BBCScousevsManc>{{cite news |first=Finlo |last=Rohrer |title=Scouse v Manc |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/magazine/6956608.stm |website=BBC News |date=21 August 2007 |access-date=3 April 2008 }}</ref>

The two clubs are [[List of football clubs by competitive honours won|the most successful in the history of English football and among the most decorated in the world]]; between them they have won 40 [[List of English football champions|league titles]], 21 [[FA Cup]]s, 16 [[EFL Cup|League Cups]], 37 [[FA Community Shield]]s, nine [[UEFA Champions League|European Cups/UEFA Champions Leagues]], four [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cups]], one [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], five [[UEFA Super Cup]]s, one [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] and two [[FIFA Club World Cup]]s. As of 3 May 2026, Liverpool lead in terms of number of trophies won with 69 to United's 68, while United lead in the head-to-head record between the two teams with 85 wins to Liverpool's 72; the remaining 61 matches have finished as draws.<ref name="goal.com">{{cite web |date=26 February 2024|title=Liverpool or Man Utd? Which UK club has won the most major trophies?|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/liverpool-man-utd-which-uk-club-have-won-most-major-trophies/eq9664p329p619x4ae81f2xff |website=Goal.com|access-date=18 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=26 February 2024|title=The five most successful English clubs in history|url=https://www.livescore.com/en/news/five-most-successful-english-clubs-liverpool-manchester-united-arsenal-chelsea-manchester-city-2024022611164493635/ |website=LiveScore|access-date=18 March 2024}}</ref><ref name="onefootball.com">{{cite web |date=17 January 2023|title=Liverpool or Man Utd? Which Premier League club has won the most trophies|url=https://onefootball.com/de/news/liverpool-or-man-utd-which-premier-league-club-has-won-the-most-trophies-36611394 |website=onefootball.com|access-date=18 March 2024}}</ref>

Neither of the two, as well as [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]], have been relegated from the [[Premier League]], the current top-tier league serving as the highest level of the English football pyramid.

==Inter-city rivals==
{{Main|Liverpool–Manchester rivalry}}
[[File:Coat of arms of Liverpool City Council.svg|thumb|The Liverpool coat of arms features the mythical bird known as the 'Liver' bird. It is believed to be based on a cormorant. This creature formed the basis of the Liverpool FC badge.]]
[[File:Arms of the City of Manchester.svg|thumb|The Manchester coat of arms formed the foundation of the original Manchester United badge.]]
The cities of [[Liverpool]] and [[Manchester]] are located in the [[North West England|north west]] of England, {{convert|35|mi|km}} apart. Since the [[Industrial Revolution]], there has been a consistent rivalry between the two cities based on economic and industrial competition. Manchester through to the 18th century was the far more populous city and was considered representative of the north. By the late 18th century, Liverpool had grown as a major seaport – critical to the growth and success of the northern cotton mills. Over the next century, Liverpool grew to supersede Manchester and throughout the late 19th and early 20th century was often described as the British Empire's [[Second city of the United Kingdom|second city]].<ref name=BBCScousevsManc/> The links between the two cities were strengthened with the construction of the [[Bridgewater Canal]], the [[Mersey and Irwell Navigation]] and the world's first inter-city railway, the [[Liverpool and Manchester Railway]], for the transport of raw materials inland.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester to Liverpool: the first inter-city railway |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/local/manchester/hi/people_and_places/history/newsid_8165000/8165208.stm |access-date=1 July 2019 |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

The construction of the [[Manchester Ship Canal]], funded by Manchester merchants, was opposed by Liverpool politicians and bred resentment between the two cities. Tensions between working-class Liverpool dockers and labourers in Manchester was heightened after its completion in 1894, just three months before the first meeting between Liverpool and Newton Heath (as United were called at the time) in a play-off match that would see Newton Heath relegated to the Second Division.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mitten |first1=Andy |title=Mad for It |year=2008 |publisher=HarperSport |location=London |isbn=978-0-00-728080-3 |pages=6–7 }}</ref>

Today, the crests of both the city of Manchester and Manchester United include stylised ships representing the Manchester Ship Canal and Manchester's trade roots. The ship is also included on the crest of many other Mancunian institutions such as the [[Manchester City Council]].

Post-war shifts in economic ties, reliance on regional coal and shifts in transatlantic trade patterns caused by the growth of Asian labour markets caused the gradual decline of British manufacturing. Both Liverpool and Manchester suffered the loss of their primary sources of income. With Liverpool, the switch from North American to continental European and Asian shipping routes tended to benefit southern English ports, while Manchester suffered from the expansion of the Asian textile industry. This reversal of fortunes happened against the backdrop of shifting political backgrounds and significant events in British culture and society in the second half of the 20th century.

Both cities were part of the county of [[Lancashire]] until 1974, with the enactment of the [[Local Government Act 1972]]. Since then, Liverpool and Manchester respectively anchor the neighbouring [[metropolitan county|metropolitan counties]] of [[Merseyside]] and [[Greater Manchester]].

The two cities continue to be strong regional rivals. Their continued importance to the UK economy has been reflected with the awarding of the [[2002 Commonwealth Games]] to Manchester, while Liverpool was awarded the title of 2008 [[European Capital of Culture]] as part of its regeneration.

More recent projects by [[Peel Ports]] have sought to re-establish the economic links between the Port of Liverpool and Port of Manchester, including re-developing trade links via the Manchester Ship Canal.

==Football rivals==
{{see also|List of Liverpool F.C. seasons|List of Manchester United F.C. seasons}}

===Formation to 1945===
[[File:ManUnited1905-1906.jpg|thumb|The Manchester United team at the start of the 1905–06 season|alt=A black-and-white photo of a football team. The players are on three levels, with four on the bottom row, four on the middle row and three on the top row. The player sitting second from the left on the bottom row has a ball at his feet, and the player in the middle of the top row is wearing a flat cap.]]
[[Manchester United F.C.]] was formed in [[Newton Heath]] in 1878 as Newton Heath LYR F.C., and played their first competitive match in October 1886, when they entered the first round of the [[1886–87 FA Cup]].<ref name="barnes_8">Barnes et al. (2001), p. 8.</ref>

[[File:Liverpool 1892-1893.jpg|thumb|Liverpool's team during its first season, 1892–93]]
[[Liverpool F.C.]] was formed in 1892 following a disagreement between the board of [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and club president [[John Houlding]], who owned the club's ground, [[Anfield]]. The disagreement between the two parties over rent resulted in Everton moving to [[Goodison Park]] from Anfield, and Houlding founded Liverpool F.C. to play in the vacated stadium. Liverpool supporters often sing the chant 'You should have paid the rent' to Everton fans during matches between the two sides, to reflect this.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/history/timeline/1892-1917/liverpool-football-club-is-formed |title=Liverpool Football Club is formed |publisher=Liverpool F.C |access-date=15 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100712112221/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/history/timeline/1892-1917/liverpool-football-club-is-formed |archive-date=12 July 2010}}</ref>

Liverpool's first season was in the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] in 1893. The team went undefeated all season, winning the title and being put up for election to the [[Football League First Division|First Division]], which would see them play a one-off [[Football League test matches|test match]] against the bottom side of the First Division for their place. The team that Liverpool were to face was Newton Heath, whom they beat 2–0 to take their place in the first tier.<ref name="rsssf1894">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1893-94.html |title=England 1893–94 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=24 February 2010 }}</ref>

Liverpool won their first [[1900–01 Football League|Football League Championship trophy in 1901]] and followed it up in [[1905–06 Football League|1906]], the same season that saw the newly renamed Manchester United promoted to the top flight after finishing as Second Division runners-up behind [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]]. Two seasons later, by which time Liverpool had fallen into mid-table, [[1907–08 Manchester United F.C. season|Manchester United secured their first league title]], winning the [[1907–08 Football League]] nine points clear of [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and Manchester City. They followed this up by winning the first-ever [[FA Charity Shield]] match when they defeated [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] over two legs in [[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Club/Trophy-Room/FA-charity.aspx|title=FA Charity / Community Shield}}</ref> The following season, they won the [[1909 FA Cup Final]], and followed this up with another [[1910–11 Football League|league title]] and [[1911 FA Charity Shield|Charity Shield]] in 1911.

The outbreak of [[World War I]] disrupted domestic football, and following the resumption of competitions in 1919 Liverpool asserted themselves on domestic football with a brace of league Championships while United found themselves in steep decline that saw them relegated in 1923. Between 1923 and the outbreak of [[World War II]], neither team won any more competitive trophies other than regional trophies, with Manchester United spending three separate periods in the Second Division.

===1945 to 1992===
[[File:Liverpool Manchester United Rivalry League Performance.svg|thumb|300px|A comparative chart showing yearly table positions of Manchester United and Liverpool in the [[English football league system]] since [[1892–93 Football League|1892–93]]|alt=refer to caption]]
After the Second World War, Liverpool again became English champions in 1947 before the clubs' roles reversed once more, with Manchester United finding stability under the management of former Liverpool captain Matt Busby, winning the [[1948 FA Cup Final|FA Cup in 1948]] and then three league titles and Charity Shields apiece in the 1950s, while the Merseysiders dropped into the second tier in 1954. During this time, future Liverpool manager [[Bill Shankly]] was approached by then Liverpool chairman [[T. V. Williams|Tom Williams]] and asked, "How would you like to manage the best club in the country?", to which Shankly replied, "Why? Is Matt Busby packing it in?"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/man-united-v-liverpool-rivalry-8271434|title=Man United v Liverpool rivalry in quotes|first=Evan|last=Bleier|date=11 December 2014|work=Manchester Evening News}}</ref>

Following Liverpool's promotion under Shankly in 1962, the two clubs found themselves in direct competition with each other for the first time, sharing four league titles between 1964 and 1967, as well as the [[1965 FA Charity Shield]]. Following this period however, the two sides began to drift in opposite directions once more. United's title victory of 1967 would be their last for 26 years,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Club/Trophy-Room.aspx |title=Trophy Room |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |access-date=29 November 2015 }}</ref> while Liverpool would enjoy 19 years of sustained success, winning 11 league titles, 19 domestic cups and seven European trophies from 1973 to 1992.<ref name="talksport.com">{{cite web|url=http://talksport.com/football/liverpool-v-man-united-which-clubs-golden-age-best-13083157895|title=Liverpool v Man United: which club's golden age is the best?|work=talkSPORT|date=31 August 2013}}</ref> United's main reprieves during this time came through cup competitions, such as their triumphs over the Merseysiders in the [[1977 FA Cup final]] and the 1979 FA Cup semi-final replay at [[Goodison Park]]. It was during this period, in the late 1970s and early 1980s, that the modern-day rivalry between the two clubs truly began to develop. According to football sociologist John Williams, Manchester United had developed a "glamour and media profile" but didn't have the success to match it, while Liverpool fans felt the Red Devils were "media darlings who got far too much publicity". There was a perception in Liverpool that their hugely successful but "professional" and "workmanlike" teams were always somehow in the shadow of the stars at Old Trafford. This led to a derisory nickname for United in Liverpool: "The Glams".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30419684|title=Man Utd v Liverpool: A strange kind of sporting love affair?|work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

===1992–present===
Manchester United's 26-year spell without a league title was replicated and exceeded by Liverpool from 1990 to 2020, during which time United dominated English football and won 13 league titles, 23 domestic cups and five European trophies.<ref name="talksport.com"/> Liverpool's success in domestic competitions such as the [[2003 Football League Cup Final|2003 League Cup]] and [[2006 FA Cup Final|2006 FA Cup]], as well as European competitions like the [[2005 UEFA Champions League Final|2005]] and [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final|2019]] Champions Leagues, allowed them some consolation during their league title dry spell, which finally ended in [[2019–20 Premier League|2020]].

Despite their contrasting fortunes, only eight times since 1972 have neither Liverpool nor United finished in the top two of the league table – in [[1980–81 Football League|1980–81]], [[2003–04 FA Premier League|2003–04]], [[2004–05 FA Premier League|2004–05]], [[2014–15 Premier League|2014–15]], [[2015–16 Premier League|2015–16]], [[2016–17 Premier League|2016–17]], [[2022–23 Premier League|2022–23]] and [[2023–24 Premier League|2023–24]] – and in seven of those eight campaigns, silverware was still taken home by one of the two clubs; Liverpool paraded the European Cup and League Cup in [[1980–81 Liverpool F.C. season|1981]], while Manchester United lifted the FA Community Shield and FA Cup in the [[2003–04 Manchester United F.C. season|2004 season]] and Liverpool claimed the Champions League in [[2004–05 Liverpool F.C. season|2005]]. United brought home the FA Cup again in [[2015–16 Manchester United F.C. season|2016]], won a treble of trophies consisting of the Community Shield, League Cup and UEFA Europa League in [[2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season|2016–17]], won the League Cup again in [[2022–23 Manchester United F.C. season|2023]] and brought back the FA Cup in [[2023–24 Manchester United F.C. season|2024]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/182119-blog-the-history-of-liverpool-man-united|title=Blog: The history of Liverpool-Man United|date=21 March 2015 |publisher=Liverpool FC}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/manchester-united/360/blog/post/3133905|title=Thanks to Europa title, Man Utd's gruelling season couldn't have ended better|website=ESPNFC.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Gravela|first=Lorenzo|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rhNCAwAAQBAJ&q=Liverpool+F.C.Manchester+United+F.C&pg=PA24|title=Soccer World - Winter Edition 2011|date=2011|publisher=Lulu.com|isbn=978-1-4477-6323-9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Man Utd 2-0 Newcastle: Erik ten Hag's side win Carabao Cup to end six-year trophy drought |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11938/12817244/man-utd-2-0-newcastle-erik-ten-hags-side-win-carabao-cup-to-end-six-year-trophy-drought |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=2024-05-25 |title=Manchester United win FA Cup after Garnacho and Mainoo stun City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/25/manchester-city-manchester-united-fa-cup-final-match-report |access-date=2024-06-29 |work=The Observer |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref>

==Managers==

===Notable managers===
{{rquote|right|''"If you are first you are first. If you are second you are nothing."''|[[Bill Shankly]]}}
While Liverpool and Manchester United's successes are almost identical in number, their systems of achieving these successes vary considerably. Liverpool built their dominance on a dynasty known as the [[The Boot Room|Anfield Boot Room]]. The boot room itself was where strategy for future matches was planned, however, it became a breeding ground for future Liverpool managers following the arrival of [[Bill Shankly]] in 1959. The original members were Shankly himself, [[Bob Paisley]], [[Joe Fagan]] and [[Reuben Bennett]], although the likes of [[Kenny Dalglish]] joined later on.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/1418093.stm|title=The legacy of the boot room|website=BBC Sport|date=21 December 2001 }}</ref> Shankly laid down principles which subsequent Boot Room graduates retained and developed: the club adopted a back four sooner than most and played a game based on possession, pushing high and [[Glossary of association football terms#P|pressing]].<ref name=philosophy>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2021/jan/23/manchester-united-lack-of-philosophy-an-advantage-chaotic-times |title=Manchester United's lack of philosophy an advantage in these chaotic times |last=Wilson |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Wilson (writer) |date=23 January 2021 |website=[[theguardian.com]] |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

Following Shankly's retirement in 1974, having secured eight trophies in 15 years, Bob Paisley stepped into the vacant manager's position and amassed 20 trophies in nine seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/history/past-managers/bob-paisley|title=Bob Paisley|website=liverpoolfc.com|publisher=Liverpool FC|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041303/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/history/past-managers/bob-paisley|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> Following his retirement, Joe Fagan took over and in the first of two seasons at the club, won a treble of trophies. Kenny Dalglish was accepted into the group as the next in line for the role of manager, and he combined it with his playing duties to win Liverpool 10 trophies. The boot room connection was finally broken in 1991, 32 years after Shankly's arrival, with the appointment of former Liverpool player [[Graeme Souness]], who demolished the original boot room itself to make way for a press room.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/lessons-manchester-united-learn-liverpools-6480610|title=The lessons for Manchester United to learn from Liverpool's demise – Manchester Evening News|first=Mike|last=Keegan|date=8 January 2014|work=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> It did still manage to produce a final Liverpool manager in [[Roy Evans]], who won the League Cup in [[1994–95 Football League Cup|1995]], but upon his resignation in 1998, the era was over. Liverpool have gone on to achieve success with managers outside of the dynasty since then, most notably under [[Rafael Benítez]], who won the [[UEFA Champions League]] in [[2005 UEFA Champions League Final|2005]], and [[Jürgen Klopp]], who won it in [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final|2019]] before going on to win the club's first league title in 30 years in [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20]]. Klopp's [[gegenpressing]] strategy has been described as a modern development of the classic Liverpool style.<ref name=philosophy />

{{rquote|right|"My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their fucking perch, and you can print that."|[[Alex Ferguson]] in response to an [[Alan Hansen]] comment in 2002<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/jan/09/sir-alex-ferguson-manchester-united-liverpool |title=The greatest challenge of Sir Alex Ferguson's career is almost over|last=Taylor |first=Daniel |date=9 January 2011 |work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=16 December 2015 |quote="My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their fucking perch, and you can print that"}}</ref>}}
By contrast, the vast majority of Manchester United's success has come in three separate eras in the club's history, under three different managers. Out of the club's 68 trophies, 56 were won under the management of [[Ernest Mangnall]], [[Matt Busby|Sir Matt Busby]] and [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]]. Mangnall was the club's first great manager, winning five trophies in three years from 1908–11.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Club/History-By-Decade/1878-to-1909.aspx |title=History by Decade }}</ref> Following his departure to local rivals Manchester City a year later,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/History/History-By-Decade/History-By-Decade/2014/Oct/manchester-united-history-1910-to-1919.aspx |title=Manchester United official history 1910 to 1919 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United}}</ref> it was not until Busby's arrival 33 years later that the club would be on the trophy trail again. Busby became United's second most decorated manager of all time (ironically as an ex-Liverpool player and captain), winning 13 trophies at the club, including the 1968 European Cup, which saw an English team secure European football's top prize for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/may/29/newsid_4464000/4464446.stm|title=BBC ON THIS DAY – 29 – 1968: Manchester Utd win European Cup|date=29 May 1968 }}</ref> After Busby's retirement in 1969 however, Manchester United saw their fortunes slip and the club struggled to stay successful until Alex Ferguson's arrival in 1986, a 17-year period in which United won only three FA Cups and two Charity Shields. It was under Ferguson that United regained their glory days, winning 38 trophies during his 26-year tenure to scale the pinnacles of both English and European football.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/manchester-united/story/2418815/sir-alex-ferguson-hopes-manchester-united-record-beaten|title=Sir Alex Ferguson hopes Manchester United record beaten – ESPN FC|work=ESPNFC.com|date=26 April 2015 }}</ref>

==Players==
===Players' rivalry===
{{rquote|right|''"A mate owned a [Manchester United captain] [[Bryan Robson]] top. We were kicking about, and I asked if I could be Robbo for a while. My dad looked out and went ballistic. He wasn't having his kid dragging the Gerrard name through the gutter. I thought we'd have to move!"''|[[Steven Gerrard]]}}
The rivalry has extended to the players as well: [[Wayne Rooney]], a product of Liverpool's city rivals [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] who played for United from 2004 to 2017, described how he grew up hating the Reds (Liverpool),<ref>{{cite web |title=Rooney: I Hate Liverpool |url=http://therepublikofmancunia.com/rooney-i-hate-liverpool/ |date=12 March 2009 |access-date=23 March 2009 }}</ref> while Liverpool's [[Steven Gerrard]] took a film crew on tour of his home where he showed off a collection of football shirts he had swapped with opposing players as part of the after-match routine; he pointed out that there were no Manchester United shirts in there and he would never have one of them in his house. Former Liverpool goalkeeper [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]] said: "I could never say I hated any United players just for being United players... But the rivalry became a habit, I suppose; on England trips Liverpool lads would eat at one table, United boys at another. There was tension there and we avoided one other". Liverpool defender [[Neil Ruddock]] once broke both of United forward [[Andy Cole]]'s legs in a reserve match, later saying that "I didn’t meant to break both legs, I only meant to break one... I absolutely destroyed him... I know it's not big and it's not clever but it was great".<ref name=lmu>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2015/oct/22/manchester-united-liverpool-class-of-92-spice-boys-eric-cantona |title=Manchester United 2–2 Liverpool: the Class of 92, Spice Boys and Cantona's return |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob|date=22 October 2015 |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref>

Manchester United's [[Gary Neville]] has been vocal about his dislike of Liverpool. He notably drew the ire of Liverpool fans during the 2006 match at Old Trafford when he celebrated [[Rio Ferdinand]]'s last-gasp winner<ref>{{cite news|title=Man Utd 1–0 Liverpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4612230.stm|website=BBC Sport|date=22 January 2006}}</ref> by running to the stand where the away fans were seated while kissing the crest on his jersey and appearing to shout angrily towards them; he was fined and given a two-match ban by [[The Football Association]] but has stated on several occasions that he has never regretted his actions.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester United news: Gary Neville says Liverpool badge-kissing celebration was 'absolutely worth' £10,000 fine|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-united-news-gary-neville-reveals-infamous-badge-kissing-in-2006-liverpool-clash-was-a7361121.html|work=[[The Independent]]|date=14 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=More Complicated Than Hate|url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/gary-neville-manchester-united-liverpool/|work=[[The Players' Tribune]]|date=16 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="NevilleCarragher2017">{{cite news|title=Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher look back on Manchester United v Liverpool clash|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/10724165/gary-neville-and-jamie-carragher-look-back-on-manchester-united-v-liverpool-clash|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=11 January 2017}}</ref> Neville was regularly subjected to offensive chants from Liverpool supporters afterwards. In a [[Manchester derby]] during the 2003–04 season, Neville was sent off after attempting to headbutt Manchester City's ex-Liverpool midfielder [[Steve McManaman]]; as [[Paul Scholes]] commented, "It's fair to say the pair of them never got on too well together".<ref name=lmu /> 

In a retrospective special leading up to the January 2017 match at Old Trafford, Neville and his fellow ''[[Monday Night Football (British TV programme)|Monday Night Football]]'' pundit and retired Liverpool one-club man [[Jamie Carragher]] both acknowledged that it was not uncommon for both United and Liverpool players, particularly locally born youth academy graduates such as [[Bury, Greater Manchester|Bury]]-born Neville and [[Merseyside]] natives Gerrard and [[Robbie Fowler]], to celebrate in front of rival fans and that "you just got to take it on the chin".<ref name="NevilleCarragher2017"/> Neville hinted that the rivalry is as much about shared values when criticising both clubs' involvement in the aborted European Super League in 2021: “I value the history and tradition that runs through those … clubs. … I don’t like them, they don’t like me, but you know one thing I always thought about them? They were honest, they had integrity, they would look after their people; they would look after their own.”<ref>{{cite AV media |date=18 April 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GP05EDm9EB8 |title="I'm absolutely DISGUSTED!" {{!}} Gary Neville's verdict on the European Super League proposals |publisher=[[Sky Sports Football]] |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=2 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824031508/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GP05EDm9EB8 |archive-date=24 August 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>
{{rquote|right|''"I can't stand Liverpool, I can't stand the people, I can't stand anything to do with them."''|[[Gary Neville]]}}
In the 2011–12 season's first league meeting of the season at Anfield, United defender [[Patrice Evra]] accused Liverpool striker [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] of racially abusing him. After considering the evidence, an FA panel found that Suárez had referred to Evra using the term "negrito" seven times (Suárez himself admitted to having done so once, but denied racism); he was banned for eight games. This included the FA Cup fourth-round tie between the two clubs (again at Anfield), which Liverpool won. 24 hours after Suarez was found guilty of racial abuse, the Liverpool players and manager wore shirts to support Suárez.<ref>{{Cite web|date=22 December 2011|title=Liverpool shirts supporting Luis Suárez 'shameful', says Paul McGrath|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/dec/22/liverpool-shirts-luis-suarez|access-date=11 December 2021|website=The Guardian}}</ref> 

On 11 February 2012, United and Liverpool met again at Old Trafford, and Suárez played for Liverpool for the first time since his ban. Before kick-off, the two teams were expected to shake hands, but Suárez ignored Evra's offered hand and moved onto the next United player in line, [[David de Gea]]. The player after De Gea, [[Rio Ferdinand]], then rejected Suárez's handshake.<ref>{{cite AV media |title=Suarez refuses Evra handshake |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/16997447 |website=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2012 |accessdate=30 January 2021 }}</ref> United went on to win 2–1 and Evra celebrated in front of the home supporters, with Suárez close by. Sir Alex Ferguson declared Suárez to be a "disgrace" and suggested that he should not be allowed to play for Liverpool again. [[Kenny Dalglish]] said he had not seen the missed handshake.<ref>{{cite news |title=Luis Suarez a 'disgrace', says Man Utd boss Sir Alex Ferguson |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16996567 |website=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2012 |accessdate=30 January 2021 }}</ref> The following day, Suárez, Dalglish and Liverpool all issued statements of apology for the handshake incident, which United accepted.<ref>{{cite news |first=Andy |last=Hunter |title=Luis Suárez misled us over Patrice Evra handshake, say angry Liverpool |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/feb/12/luis-suarez-patrice-evra-liverpool-apologies |work=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News & Media |date=12 February 2012 |accessdate=30 January 2021 }}</ref> 

Liverpool's vice-captain for the 2011–12 season, [[Jamie Carragher]], later apologised to Evra in 2019 for wearing shirts in support of Suarez, saying '"There's no doubt we made a massive mistake. I'm not lying on that and saying I wasn't part of it because as the club we got it wrong and I was vice-captain. I'm not sure who was actually behind it".<ref>{{Cite news|date=22 October 2019|title=Liverpool made 'massive mistake' in backing Luis Suarez in the 2011 racism row, admits Jamie Carragher|work=The Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/10/22/liverpool-made-massive-mistake-backing-luis-suarez-2011-racism/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/10/22/liverpool-made-massive-mistake-backing-luis-suarez-2011-racism/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=11 December 2021|issn=0307-1235}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Similarly in 2020 [[Jordan Henderson]], a young Liverpool player at the time of the incident who went on to captain the club, stated in an interview for a [[BBC]] documentary on football and racism that he was "not sure the club or everybody dealt with it in the best way. From a player point of view, our mindset was on Luis and how to protect him, but really we didn't really think about Patrice. I think that's where we got it wrong from top to bottom".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/henderson-evra-suarez-liverpool-shirts-19349114 |title=Jordan Henderson admits Liverpool 'got it wrong' with Luis Suarez t-shirt support |last=O'Neill |first=Connor |date=26 November 2020 |website=[[liverpoolecho.co.uk]] |access-date=6 November 2022}}</ref>

===Player transfers===
[[File:Michael Owen Johnny Heitinga cropped (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Michael Owen]] is the most recent player to play for both clubs.]]
Since the 1964 transfer of [[Phil Chisnall]] from United to Liverpool, no player has been transferred directly between the two clubs.<ref>{{cite news |title=The day that Phil crossed the great divide! |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/07/06/the-day-that-phil-crossed-the-great-divide--100252-19412368/ |work=[[Liverpool Echo]] |date=6 July 2007 |access-date=9 July 2007 }}</ref> Some players, however, have played for both clubs but played elsewhere between each tenure, such as [[Paul Ince]] (playing for [[Inter Milan]] in between), [[Peter Beardsley]] ([[Vancouver Whitecaps (NASL)|Vancouver Whitecaps]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]) and more recently [[Michael Owen]] ([[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] and Newcastle United). Although Beardsley only played once for United, he went on to be a key player during his four years at Liverpool.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/8131801.stm|title=Owen completes switch to Man Utd |date=3 July 2009|website=BBC Sport|access-date=4 July 2009}}</ref>

In 2007, there was a bid from Liverpool to sign [[Gabriel Heinze]] from United, but United refused to allow him to join their biggest rivals due to the ongoing feud. United claimed that it was agreed Heinze would only join a foreign club if he chose to leave.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thesoccerblog.org/premiership/liverpool-eyeing-heinze/ |website=thesoccerblog.org |title=Liverpool Eyeing Heinze |date=3 July 2007 |access-date=9 July 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928115621/http://www.thesoccerblog.org/premiership/liverpool-eyeing-heinze/ |archive-date=28 September 2007 }}</ref> Heinze went public with his request to join Liverpool which was seen as the ultimate betrayal by the Manchester United fans. The Manchester United fans who once chanted "Argentina" in honour of the player then turned their backs on him. Heinze was eventually sold to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] instead. In 2019, after Swedish striker [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] left [[LA Galaxy]], Liverpool manager [[Jürgen Klopp]] said that he might have considered signing Ibrahimović had he not previously played for Manchester United.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/soccer/liverpool-engliverpool/story/3990395/zlatan-ibrahimovics-link-to-man-united-prevented-liverpool-move-klopp Zlatan Ibrahimovic's link to Man United prevented Liverpool move - Klopp], ESPN.com, 15 November 2019</ref>

==Supporters==
{{main|Supporters' groups|Association football culture}}
[[File:Liverpool v Chelsea, 2005.jpg|thumb|Liverpool ''Kopites'' in [[Spion Kop (stadiums)|The Kop]] stand at [[Anfield]]|alt=A single tiered stand that contains thousands of people. Several flags are being waved. In front of the stand is a grass pitch with a goal.]]
Both Manchester United and Liverpool are among the most popular football clubs (and sporting organisations) globally. Both are in the top 10 in Europe. Manchester United states that its worldwide fan base includes more than 320 officially recognised branches of the Manchester United Supporters Club (MUSC) in at least 90 countries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man Utd Supporters Clubs |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/fans/supporters-clubs-directory?id=menu |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |access-date=31 December 2024}}</ref> Liverpool states that its worldwide fan base also includes more than 300 officially recognised branches of the Official LFC Supporters Clubs (OLSCs) in over 100 countries.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official LFC Supporters Clubs |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/fans/official-lfc-supporters-clubs |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240817161438/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/fans/official-lfc-supporters-clubs |archive-date=17 August 2024 |access-date=31 December 2024}}</ref> Notable groups include [[Spirit of Shankly]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/fans/membership/aib-association-of-international-branches |title=LFC Official Supporters Clubs |publisher=Liverpool F.C |access-date=6 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723160733/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/fans/membership/aib-association-of-international-branches |archive-date=23 July 2011 }}</ref>

The 2005 leveraged takeover of Manchester United by [[Glazer ownership of Manchester United|the Glazer family]] created a schism amongst Manchester fans, directly causing the creation of [[F.C. United of Manchester]], and the "Love United Hate Glazer" movement, and subsequently the Red Knights who attempted to buy the Glazers out the club.<ref>{{cite web |first=Matt |last=Rickard |title=United We Stand |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/feature?id=336636&cc=5739 |publisher=ESPN |date=5 July 2005 |access-date=12 July 2005 |archive-date=12 February 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212174901/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/feature?id=336636&cc=5739 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |first=Robert |last=Brady |year=2006 |title=An Undividable Glow – The story of FCUM's first season |publisher=Robert Brady |isbn=978-0-9553620-0-2 }}</ref> Two years later, Liverpool went through its own controversial takeover when Chairman [[David Moores]] sold the club to American businessmen George Gillett and Tom Hicks.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/6244441.stm |first=Bill |last=Wilson |title=US business duo at Liverpool helm |publisher=BBC |date=6 February 2007 |access-date=2 December 2008 }}</ref> Disagreements between Gillett and Hicks, and the lack of popular support from fans, resulted in the pair looking to sell the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/7197675.stm |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Liverpool braced for takeover bid |work=BBC Sport |date=20 January 2008 |access-date=2 December 2008 }}</ref> [[Martin Broughton]] was appointed chairman of the club on 16 April 2010 to oversee its sale.<ref name="broughtonchair">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/apr/16/martin-broughton-liverpool-chairman-sale|title=Liverpool appoint Martin Broughton as chairman to oversee sale of club|last=Bandini|first=Nicky|date=16 April 2010|work=The Guardian|access-date=16 April 2010}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/may/07/liverpool-record-losses|title=Auditors cast doubt on future of Liverpool after losses|date=7 May 2010|work=The Guardian|access-date=8 May 2010|first=David|last=Conn}}</ref> Court action finally forced the sale of the club to Fenway Sports Group.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=831953&sec=england&cc=4716 |title=Liverpool takeover to go ahead as owners lose case |publisher=ESPN |date=13 October 2010 |access-date=23 March 2011 |archive-date=16 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101016070447/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=831953&sec=england&cc=4716 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/9094283.stm |title=Liverpool takeover completed by US company NESV |work=BBC Sport |date=15 October 2010 |access-date=12 August 2011}}</ref>

===Hooliganism===
{{main|Football hooliganism}}
With the rise of [[football hooliganism]] across English football during the 1970s and 1980s, matches between the two clubs brought some minor and major incidents of hooliganism.{{citation needed|date=January 2009}} Since then, the modern game has seen a decrease in violence between the rival supporters and incidents are fairly uncommon. This is more likely due to an increase in Police presence and CCTV with huge steps taken to keep the fans separated. To this day, both sets of fans still hold resentment toward each other. As well as physical violence, sections of the clubs' fan bases often taunt each other with unsavoury chants about the [[Munich air disaster]] and the [[Hillsborough disaster]] respectively.

At the [[1996 FA Cup final]], an unidentified Liverpool fan spat at [[Eric Cantona]] and threw a punch at Alex Ferguson as a victorious Manchester United team walked up the steps at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] to collect the [[FA Cup|trophy]] from the Royal Box.<ref name="IND14824533">{{cite news |title=Wembley to act over spitting |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/wembley-to-act-over-spitting-1346999.html |work=[[The Independent]] |date=13 May 1996 |access-date=17 January 2009 |location=London}}</ref>

The 2006 FA Cup match at Anfield featured foreign objects thrown at United fans by Liverpool supporters, including human excrement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Anfield Admits Excrement Thrown at Utd Fans|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=362170&cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716090210/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=362170&cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 July 2012|work=ESPN Soccernet|publisher=ESPN|access-date=26 August 2011}}</ref> Liverpool's [[FA Cup semi-final]] game against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Old Trafford]] later that year also resulted in damage to the stadium, including graffiti about serial killer [[Harold Shipman]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rival Fans Vandalise Old Trafford|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/manchester/4943290.stm|website=BBC News|access-date=26 August 2011|date=25 April 2006}}</ref>

In March 2011, an FA Youth Cup game between the two clubs was marred because of "sick chants" about Hillsborough and [[Heysel Stadium disaster|Heysel]] coming from the Manchester United fans at Anfield. Former Liverpool striker [[John Aldridge]] was at the game and told the ''[[Liverpool Echo]]'' that "the level of abuse was absolutely sickening".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/8380303/Former-Liverpool-striker-John-Aldridge-slams-Manchester-United-fans-who-marred-Youth-Cup-game.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/8380303/Former-Liverpool-striker-John-Aldridge-slams-Manchester-United-fans-who-marred-Youth-Cup-game.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Daily Telegraph |title=Former Liverpool striker John Aldridge slams Manchester United fans who marred Youth Cup game |date=14 March 2011 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

In March 2016, before Liverpool's first leg tie at Anfield against Manchester United in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]], it was reported that a group of Liverpool fans hung a "Manc Bastards" banner on the [[M62 motorway|M62]], as 2,300 Manchester United supporters made the trip to Anfield.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.givemesport.com/728246-liverpool-fans-unveil-abusive-banner-towards-manchester-united-fans-on-motorway|title=Liverpool fans unveil abusive banner towards Manchester United fans on motorway|date=11 March 2016|website=GiveMeSport}}</ref> It was confiscated by the police, shortly after. Liverpool won the match [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Liverpool v Manchester United|2–0]]. Before the second leg tie at Old Trafford, Liverpool fans were greeted with a banner on the M62 in Salford that said 'murderers' and also had the Hillsborough disaster's date on it. UEFA took no disciplinary action against Manchester United.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/mar/17/liverpool-hillsborough-manchester-united-fans-murderers-europa-league|title=Liverpool supporters welcomed to Manchester with 'murderers' banner|last=Dobson|first=Mark|date=17 March 2016|newspaper=The Guardian|issn=0261-3077|access-date=18 March 2016}}</ref> During the same game, there were reported crowd disturbances, coming from the Manchester United end.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/manchester-united-liverpool-fans-clash-7580435|title=Man United and Liverpool fans clash inside Old Trafford during Europa League tie|first=James|last=Whaling|date=18 March 2016|website=The mirror}}</ref> It was later reported that a Liverpool supporter snuck a Liverpool banner into the United section, aggravating United supporters in the stands.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/reason-manchester-united-liverpool-fans-7581048|title=Is this the reason Man United and Liverpool fans clashed inside Old Trafford?|first=Hamish|last=Mackay|date=19 March 2016|website=The Mirror}}</ref> Liverpool supporters ripped out seats, and supporters threw objects at each other, also fighting with United supporters. Liverpool were fined £43,577 by UEFA for setting off flares and fireworks in the crowd, as well as the singing of "illicit chants", while Manchester United were fined £44,342 for illicit chants and the throwing of objects.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36372274|title=Uefa fines Liverpool and Manchester United for illicit chants|date=24 May 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> £15,290 of each club's fine was suspended for two years. The match was drawn [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Manchester United v Liverpool|1–1]] and Liverpool progressed to the quarter-finals against [[Borussia Dortmund]].

In August 2022, ITV reported that some Manchester United fans attacked a bus en route to Old Trafford, in the belief it was transporting the Liverpool team or fans; it was actually carrying children who supported Manchester United.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.itv.com/news/granada/2022-08-23/manchester-united-fans-pelt-bus-carrying-children-with-bottles |title=Manchester United fans pelt bus carrying children with bottles |date=23 August 2022 }}</ref>

In May 2023, shortly after the [[2023 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]] between Manchester United and Manchester City, a photograph emerged online of a United supporter wearing a kit with the words "Not Enough" and the number 97 printed on the back, a mockery of the Hillsborough disaster. The supporter was later identified and arrested following the attention the photo received, and was fined £1000 and given a 4-year ban from attending regulated football games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Man arrested at FA Cup final for wearing offensive Hillsborough shirt |url=https://news.sky.com/story/man-arrested-at-fa-cup-final-for-wearing-offensive-hillsborough-shirt-12895849 |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=Sky News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Parker-Turner |first=Charlie |date=20 June 2023 |title=Man Utd ban man who wore '97 not enough' shirt to mock Hillsborough disaster |url=https://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/1782360/Man-Utd-ban-Hillsborough-shirt-FA-Cup |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=Express.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Significant games==

===1894 test match===
The first-ever meeting between both clubs came in a [[Football League test matches#1894|Football League test match]] in 1894, a post-season series to determine who would receive [[Football League First Division|First Division]] membership for [[1894–95 Football League|1894–95]]. As Newton Heath finished bottom of the First Division at the end of [[1893–94 Football League|1893–94]], they had to play off against the champions of the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]], Liverpool. Liverpool won the tie 2–0 at [[Ewood Park]] in [[Blackburn]], earning them First Division membership and condemning Newton Heath to the Second Division.

===1977 FA Cup final===
In 1977, the two clubs met in a cup final for the first time, when they reached the [[1977 FA Cup final|final]] of the [[FA Cup]]. The two clubs took to the field at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] on 21 May, with Liverpool having just won the league title, knowing that winning this game would put them on course for a unique [[Treble (association football)|treble]] as they had the [[1977 European Cup final|European Cup final]] to look forward to four days later. However, United ended Liverpool's treble dreams with a 2–1 win, with goals from [[Stuart Pearson]] and [[Jimmy Greenhoff]], five minutes apart with a [[Jimmy Case]] goal for Liverpool in between.

===1983 Football League Cup final===
Six years later, on 26 March 1983, the two sides met for the [[1983 Football League Cup final|Football League Cup final]]. Goals from [[Alan Kennedy]] and [[Ronnie Whelan]] won the game 2–1 for Liverpool, after [[Norman Whiteside]] had given United the lead. Liverpool collected the trophy for the third year in succession. It was the last of Liverpool manager [[Bob Paisley]]'s nine seasons in charge (during which Liverpool had dominated the English and European scene) before his retirement, and his players allowed him to climb the 39 steps to collect the trophy from the Royal Box.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Managers/Manager/Profile/10|title=Bob Paisley – LFChistory – Stats galore for Liverpool FC!}}</ref>

===Anfield 1988===
On 4 April 1988, Liverpool were 11 points ahead at the top of the league and almost certain of winning the First Division title with barely a month of the league season remaining. United, in their first full season under the management of Alex Ferguson, were their nearest rivals. The two sides took to the field for a league encounter at Anfield and with the second half just minutes old the home side had a 3–1 lead with goals from [[Peter Beardsley]], [[Gary Gillespie]] and [[Steve McMahon]], with United's only goal coming from [[Bryan Robson]]. Robson then pulled a goal back for United, and with 12 minutes remaining fellow midfielder [[Gordon Strachan]] equalised to force a 3–3 draw.<ref name="insda">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/classic-liverpool-v-manchester-united-encounters-1807274.html?action=Gallery |title=Classic Liverpool v Manchester United encounters |location=London |work=The Independent |first=Simon |last=Rice |date=4 March 2011 }}</ref>

===Other notable games===
On 4 January 1994, in the second season of the new [[Premier League]], United took a 3–0 lead at Anfield in the opening 25 minutes with goals from [[Steve Bruce]], [[Ryan Giggs]] and [[Denis Irwin]]. Liverpool managed to claw back to draw 3–3 with two goals from [[Nigel Clough]] and another from [[Neil Ruddock]]. It was one of the last games in charge of Liverpool for manager [[Graeme Souness]], who had resigned by the end of the month.<ref name="insda"/>

On 1 October 1995, United's [[Eric Cantona]] made his comeback to the side after serving an eight-month suspension for attacking a spectator in a game against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. His comeback game was against Liverpool in the Premier League at Old Trafford. United took an early lead through [[Nicky Butt]], only for Liverpool's [[Robbie Fowler]] to score twice and give the visitors a 2–1 lead. However, United were awarded a penalty in the 71st minute and Cantona converted it successfully, forcing a 2–2 draw.<ref name="insda"/> At the end of the season, the two sides met again at Wembley for the [[1996 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]]. The game stayed goalless until the 85th minute, when Liverpool conceded a corner, which [[David Beckham]] swung into the box to be cleared by [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]], only for Eric Cantona to fire home United's winner.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/4694012.stm |website=BBC Sport |first=Ian |last=Wilkerson |title=FA Cup flashback |date=16 February 2006}}</ref> In March 2003, the two clubs once again met in a cup final, this time in the [[2003 Football League Cup final|League Cup]], with Liverpool lifting the trophy after goals from [[Steven Gerrard]] and [[Michael Owen]] gave them a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool lift Worthington Cup |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/2811805.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=2 March 2003 |access-date=22 March 2015 }}</ref>

On 14 March 2009, the two sides met at Old Trafford in the Premier League. United were ahead at the top of the league and Liverpool were looking to make a late run to the title which had eluded them since 1990. United went ahead in the 23rd minute with a [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] penalty, but [[Fernando Torres]] equalised five minutes later for Liverpool, and a [[Steven Gerrard]] penalty just before half-time put Liverpool in the lead. United had [[Nemanja Vidić]] sent off in the 76th minute, and their misery was swiftly compounded by late goals from [[Fábio Aurélio]] and finally [[Andrea Dossena]], condemning them to a 4–1 defeat, their heaviest at Old Trafford in any competition for 17 years.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7922069.stm |website=BBC Sport |title=Man Utd 1–4 Liverpool |date=14 March 2009 }}</ref> Despite the loss, Manchester United were crowned league champions for the third season in succession and equalled Liverpool's 18 league titles,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8038259.stm |website=BBC Sport |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 0–0 Arsenal |date=18 May 2009 }}</ref> with Liverpool finishing four points behind in second.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8048312.stm |website=BBC Sport |first=Oliver |last=Brett |title=Liverpool 3–1 Tottenham |date=24 May 2009 }}</ref>

The league fixture on 11 February 2012 was marked by controversy regarding Liverpool striker [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] refusal to shake hands with [[Patrice Evra]], following an eight-match suspension for racially abusing Evra in the previous meeting between the sides.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16186556|website=BBC Sport|title=Liverpool striker Luis Suarez handed eight-match ban|date=20 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16884839|website=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty|title=Man Utd 2–1 Liverpool|date=11 February 2012}}</ref> Following the 2–1 victory for United after a brace from [[Wayne Rooney]], Evra in turn controversially celebrated right in front of Suárez, and was swept aside by opposition players finding the gesture provocative.

In the 2015–16 season the two rivals faced each other for the first time on the European stage, in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16]] of the [[UEFA Europa League]]. Liverpool won the tie 3–1 on aggregate with a 2–0 victory at Anfield on 10 March 2016<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool 2-0 Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35763810|first=Phil |last=McNulty |access-date=6 March 2023|date=10 March 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> and the sides drawing 1–1 at Old Trafford seven days later.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester United 1-1 Liverpool (agg 1-3)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35815538|first=Phil |last=McNulty |access-date=6 March 2023|date=17 March 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |date=6 December 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5A8k1wadIw |title=#UEL Fixture Flashback: Liverpool 3-1 Manchester United |publisher=[[UEFA]] |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=2 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124095859/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5A8k1wadIw |archive-date=24 January 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> Liverpool would go on to reach the [[2016 UEFA Europa League final|final]], losing 3–1 to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool 1-3 Sevilla|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36254631|first=Phil |last=McNulty |access-date=6 March 2023|date=18 May 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 24 October 2021, Manchester United suffered their heaviest ever home defeat to Liverpool, as a [[Mohamed Salah]] hat-trick – the first by a Liverpool player at Old Trafford since [[Fred Howe (footballer, born 1912)|Fred Howe]] in [[1936–37 Football League#First Division|November 1936]] – and goals from [[Naby Keïta]] and [[Diogo Jota]] gave Liverpool a 5–0 win in the [[2021–22 Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Manchester United 0-5 Liverpool: Salah hat-trick as Solskjaer's side thrashed |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58943625 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2021 |access-date=27 October 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first1=Duncan |last1=Alexander|first2=Matt|last2=Furniss|url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2021/10/the-data-day-no-11-our-rolling-football-blog/|date=24 October 2021|title=The Data Day No. 11: Our Rolling Football Blog|access-date=6 March 2023|work=Opta Analyst}}</ref> Salah's hat-trick was the first scored by an away team at Old Trafford since [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]]'s in [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Manchester United vs Real Madrid|April 2003]] and the first hat-trick scored there by an away team in the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mo Salah becomes first away player to score Premier League hat-trick at Man Utd|editor-first=Barney |editor-last=Corkhill |url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/man-utd/news/salah-becomes-first-away-player-to-score-premier-league-hat-trick-at-man-utd_468252.html |access-date=24 October 2021|date=24 October 2021 |website=SportsMole }}</ref>

On 5 March 2023, Liverpool recorded their biggest ever competitive win against Manchester United with a 7–0 victory at Anfield. [[Cody Gakpo]], [[Darwin Núñez]] and Mohamed Salah each scored a brace, with [[Roberto Firmino]] adding on a seventh. This surpassed their previous record set in October 1895, a 7–1 victory in the [[1895–96 Football League#Second Division|Second Division]]. This was also Manchester United's [[List of Manchester United F.C. records and statistics#Record defeats|joint-biggest ever defeat]] and the heaviest since [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] beat them by the same scoreline in [[1931–32 Football League#Second Division|1931]].<ref name="BBC5323">{{cite news |last=McNulty|first=Phil |title=Liverpool 7-0 Manchester United: Reds thrash old rivals in Anfield rout|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64775037|access-date=5 March 2023|work=BBC Sport |date=5 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Liverpool thrash Manchester United 7-0 in historic defeat |url=https://news.sky.com/story/liverpool-thrash-man-united-7-0-in-historic-defeat-12826896 |first=Andy |last=Hayes |access-date=5 March 2023|date=5 March 2023|website=Sky News }}</ref> Despite this result, Liverpool finished the season in fifth place, eight points behind third-placed Manchester United.<ref>{{cite web |title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives {{!}} 2022/23 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=489&ha=-1 |website=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |accessdate=25 May 2025 }}</ref>

===Women's football results===
Following the creation of [[Manchester United W.F.C.]] in 2018, the rivalry has now appeared in women's football as matches between the sides are now possible. [[Liverpool F.C. Women]] was created in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64239954|title=Manchester United v Liverpool: Women's teams can 'build history' of rivalry in WSL|access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45181889|title=Manchester United mark return to women's football with a new Liverpool rivalry|access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref>
